entry_lifecycle.catalyst_logic: The hold is already printed; the leftover is persistence of the US-Japan policy gap versus an unowned mid-range USDJPY book, exhausted if Japan hikes or the United States cash rate converges.
entry_lifecycle.realization_logic: Dollar-yen grinds higher as the 271 basis-point SOFR-TONA cash gap and the March 2027 4.39 versus 1.67 path gap keep paying after a hold, not as a one-day devaluation spike.

entry_rationale: The Bank of Japan hold is spent, SOFR 3.94 versus TONA 1.227 remains unowned in spot, and this size is a from-zero initiation rather than a USDCAD re-entry against WTI 102.
entry_thesis: The Bank of Japan held, so the dated yen event that kept dollar-yen unowned is spent, and the leftover still sits in a 271 basis-point SOFR 3.94 versus TONA 1.227 cash gap and a 272 basis-point March SOFR 4.39 versus March TONA 1.67 path gap. Long USDJPY at the 158.06 paper mid is the cleanest from-zero dollar expression: the pair is at a one-year z-score of 0.02, not a chase. Dollar-Canada at 1.3996 is not that ticket while WTI is 102, Brent is 114.88, Canada's oil-pressure proxy is rising, and there is no Bank of Canada headline; short euro-dollar at 1.113 would fade a one-year z-score of -2.60 rather than own the Japan leftover.

events.rationale: The Bank of Japan hold is spent, SOFR 3.94 versus TONA 1.227 remains unowned in spot, and this size is a from-zero initiation rather than a USDCAD re-entry against WTI 102.

invalidation: The long is wrong if a later freeze shows the Bank of Japan hiking and TONA catching the March contract from the Japan side, or if official SOFR converges toward TONA so the overnight gap closes from the United States side. A Ministry of Finance intervention print that reverses the post-hold leftover also kills it. Three-digit oil is not this ticket's invalidation; it is why USDCAD stays flat.
